title: Visual director output: one constructed scene per narration beat
description: Contract between the visual director (scripts/visual-director/direct.mjs), the material resolver (scripts/visual-director/materials/), the shot renderer (src/skills/remotion-render/shots/) and the critic loop (scripts/visual-director/critic.mjs). A scene is CONSTRUCTED from the sentence's meaning: semantic model -> visual question -> mechanism -> shots -> materials -> camera -> animation -> typography. There is no field that selects a component or a 'visual type'. See docs/VISUAL-DIRECTOR.md.

script.description: repo-relative path of the script JSON this direction was made from

reference.description: stem of the reference analysis consulted (data/reference/analysis/<stem>), null when none

semantic.description: What the sentence MEANS, before any visual is considered. Each field is a short plain-language phrase grounded in the sentence; null when the sentence genuinely has none.

visual_question.description: the question an excellent motion designer asks of THIS sentence, e.g. 'how do you show a fragment physically cut out of a 70-metre cloth?'

family.description: the verb of the scene. 'statement' = typography carries the beat; capped (docs/VISUAL-DIRECTOR.md).

construction.description: the one-off scene this sentence needs, described concretely: which real things, what happens to them, in what space

why.description: why this mechanism communicates this sentence's relationship/change, tied to the semantic fields

mute_test.description: what a viewer with the sound OFF understands from this scene alone

evidence.description: source URLs (from the script's sources_used) that ground the fact this scene shows

reference_cues.description: reference observations this scene borrows technique from, cited as '<stem>#fNNN'. Technique only, never content.

from.description: framing at shot start, e.g. 'extreme close on the cut edge of the cloth'

motivation.description: why the camera moves this way FOR THIS mechanism (reveal -> close then pull out; scale -> detail then wide)

action.description: what physically happens to the materials during the shot (the mechanism in motion)

text.description: typography SUPPORTS the image; it never substitutes for it

sync_word.description: the narration word the text lands on

sfx.description: a sound tied to a visual event in this shot, or null

must_show.description: what the picture must literally depict for this scene to work, e.g. 'the Bayeux Tapestry panel with Halley's comet'

search.description: search queries for licensed sources (Wikimedia Commons first)

data.description: only for kind=data: the sourced values a genuine quantity comparison needs

resolved.description: written by the material resolver, never by the director

verdict.description: the vision verifier's one-line answer to must_show
